subproblem.title: Finite C¹ partition of unity on a neighbourhood of a compact set, subordinate to locally given open sets
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, C ⊆ ℝᴺ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) compact, and P a property of subsets of ℝᴺ such that every y ∈ C lies in some open set U with P(U). Then there exist p ∈ ℕ, functions ζ_q : ℝᴺ → ℝ (q ∈ Fin p) and an open set O ⊇ C such that Σ_q ζ_q(z) = 1 for every z ∈ O, and for every q: ζ_q is C¹, ζ_q has compact support, and tsupport ζ_q ⊆ U for some U with P(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (C : Set (Rn N)) (P : Set (Rn N) → Prop), IsCompact C → (∀ y ∈ C, ∃ U : Set (Rn N), IsOpen U ∧ y ∈ U ∧ P U) → ∃ (p : ℕ) (ζ : Fin p → Rn N → ℝ) (O : Set (Rn N)), IsOpen O ∧ C ⊆ O ∧ (∀ z ∈ O, ∑ q, ζ q z = 1) ∧ ∀ q, ContDiff ℝ 1 (ζ q) ∧ HasCompactSupport (ζ q) ∧ ∃ U : Set (Rn N), P U ∧ tsupport (ζ q) ⊆ U
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3a–3b of the supplied proof of the parent node root.stationary_results-a1.divergence_identity-a1 (a finite cover of M ∩ S by balls inside chart targets, and the bump-product partition of unity ζ_q = β_q ∏_{l<q}(1 − β_l)), stated for an arbitrary compact C and property P.

Notation: B(c, ρ) is the open ball and B̄(c, ρ) the closed ball in ℝᴺ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N).

1. (Local radii.) For each y ∈ C choose an open set U_y with y ∈ U_y and P(U_y). Since U_y is open, choose ε_y > 0 with B(y, ε_y) ⊆ U_y (Metric.isOpen_iff).

2. (Finite subcover.) For y ∈ C the ball B(y, ε_y/4) is a neighbourhood of y. By compactness of C (IsCompact.elim_nhds_subcover) there is a finite set T ⊆ C with C ⊆ ⋃_{y ∈ T} B(y, ε_y/4).
 - Let p := #T and enumerate T as c_0, …, c_{p−1}, indexed by q ∈ Fin p (e.g. via Finset.equivFin).
 - Write ε_q := ε_{c_q} > 0.
 - Put O := ⋃_q B(c_q, ε_q/4). O is open, being a union of open balls, and C ⊆ O.

3. (Bumps.) For each q let β_q be the smooth bump function centred at c_q with inner radius ε_q/4 and outer radius ε_q/2 (Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = ε_q/4, rOut = ε_q/2; note 0 < ε_q/4 < ε_q/2). Then:
 - β_q : ℝᴺ → ℝ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff);
 - β_q = 1 on B̄(c_q, ε_q/4) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall);
 - tsupport β_q = B̄(c_q, ε_q/2) (ContDiffBump.tsupport_eq);
 - β_q has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport).

4. (Definition.) Set ζ_q(x) := β_q(x) · ∏_{l ∈ Fin p, l < q} (1 − β_l(x)).

5. (Regularity and support.)
 - ζ_q is C¹, indeed C^∞, as the product of β_q with a finite product of the C^∞ functions 1 − β_l (ContDiff.mul, contDiff_prod).
 - Since ζ_q = β_q · (…), support ζ_q ⊆ support β_q. Hence tsupport ζ_q ⊆ tsupport β_q = B̄(c_q, ε_q/2) (tsupport_mul_subset_left), which is contained in B(c_q, ε_q) because ε_q/2 < ε_q (closedBall_subset_ball), which is contained in U_{c_q}. And P(U_{c_q}) holds.
 - ζ_q has compact support because β_q does (HasCompactSupport.mul_right).

6. (Telescoping identity.) For any real numbers b_0, …, b_{p−1}, ∏_q (1 − b_q) = 1 − Σ_q b_q ∏_{l<q} (1 − b_l) (Finset.prod_one_sub_ordered).
 Proof by induction on the finite index set s: if m is the largest index of s, then ∏_{q∈s}(1 − b_q) = (1 − b_m) ∏_{q∈s∖{m}}(1 − b_q) = ∏_{q∈s∖{m}}(1 − b_q) − b_m ∏_{l∈s, l<m}(1 − b_l), and the induction hypothesis for s ∖ {m} gives the claim.
 With b_q := β_q(z) this says Σ_q ζ_q(z) = 1 − ∏_q (1 − β_q(z)) for every z.

7. (The sum equals one on O.) Let z ∈ O. Then z ∈ B(c_q, ε_q/4) ⊆ B̄(c_q, ε_q/4) for some q, so β_q(z) = 1 by step 3. The factor 1 − β_q(z) vanishes, so ∏_l (1 − β_l(z)) = 0 (Finset.prod_eq_zero), and by step 6, Σ_q ζ_q(z) = 1.

8. (Conclusion.) Steps 2, 5 and 7 give all the asserted properties of p, (ζ_q) and O. If C = ∅ the construction gives T = ∅, p = 0 and O = ∅, and the assertions hold vacuously. ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ C choose an open U_y with P(U_y) and ε_y > 0 with B(y, ε_y) ⊆ U_y. Extract a finite subcover of C by the balls B(c_q, ε_q/4) and let O be their union.
Take the ContDiffBump β_q at c_q with rIn = ε_q/4, rOut = ε_q/2 and set ζ_q = β_q ∏_{l<q}(1 − β_l). Each ζ_q is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ζ_q ⊆ B̄(c_q, ε_q/2) ⊆ U_{c_q}.
By telescoping (Finset.prod_one_sub_ordered), Σ_q ζ_q = 1 − ∏_q(1 − β_q), which equals 1 on O because some β_q = 1 at each point of O.

audit.reason: The finite subcover, explicit bump radii, support containment, and telescoping product identity establish every asserted output. The construction handles empty C and zero-dimensional ambient space. The frozen proposition precisely states the requested C¹ conclusion and is independently usable; no further proof search or planning is needed.
